_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mozambique covering Bantu migration, Swahili coast trading, Great Zimbabwe trade links, Portuguese colonisation (longest in Africa 1498-1975), FRELIMO liberation war, civil war 1977-1992, economic growth, and Cabo Delgado insurgency.

ethnic_groups.name: Makhuwa (Makua)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; northern Mozambique; Nampula and Cabo Delgado; matrilineal; coastal and interior sub-groups

ethnic_groups.name: Tsonga (Shangaan/Ronga)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Mozambique; Gaza and Maputo provinces; related to South African Tsonga; historical Gaza kingdom

ethnic_groups.name: Lomwe
ethnic_groups.notes: Zambézia province; related to Malawi Lomwe; tea plantations

ethnic_groups.name: Sena
ethnic_groups.notes: Zambezi valley; Sofala and Tete; prazos system legacy

ethnic_groups.name: Nyanja/Chewa
ethnic_groups.notes: Tete province; cross-border with Malawi; Maravi heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Yao
ethnic_groups.notes: Niassa province; Muslim; historical slave traders; cross-border with Malawi/Tanzania

ethnic_groups.name: Makonde
ethnic_groups.notes: Cabo Delgado plateau; famous woodcarvers; matrilineal; FRELIMO heartland; cross-border with Tanzania

ethnic_groups.name: Ndau
ethnic_groups.notes: Sofala; historically resisted Portuguese; RENAMO support base

ethnic_groups.name: Swahili/Mwani
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern coast; Islamic; Ilha de Moçambique heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Ngoni
ethnic_groups.notes: Niassa and Tete; Nguni invaders (Mfecane); Gaza state

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Tonga, Chopi, Marenje, Asian, European)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indians, Portuguese, Chinese; various smaller Bantu groups

current_leader.name: Filipe Nyusi
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: FRELIMO; former defense minister; presided over gas boom and Cabo Delgado insurgency; term-limited 2024

president_elect.name: Daniel Chapo
president_elect.title: President-elect
president_elect.notes: FRELIMO; won disputed 2024 election; takes office January 2025; youngest president at 47

former_presidents.name: Samora Machel
former_presidents.notes: First president; FRELIMO liberation hero; Marxist-Leninist; died in suspicious plane crash in South Africa

former_presidents.name: Joaquim Chissano
former_presidents.notes: Transitioned from socialism to market economy; ended civil war (Rome Accord 1992); Mo Ibrahim Prize 2007

former_presidents.name: Armando Guebuza
former_presidents.notes: FRELIMO; businessman; hidden debt scandal legacy; coal and gas development era

910.name: Early Peoples and Bantu Migration
910.description: San hunter-gatherer habitation followed by Bantu migration introducing agriculture, ironworking, and new social structures.

sub_clusters.name: San Hunter-Gatherer Communities
sub_clusters.description: Early Stone Age and Later Stone Age San peoples inhabiting the region; rock art evidence.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration into Mozambique
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate southward bringing iron smelting, agriculture, and cattle-keeping.

920.name: Swahili Coast Trading Cities
920.description: Rise of Swahili trading settlements on the Mozambican coast; gold and ivory trade linking interior kingdoms to Indian Ocean commerce.

sub_clusters.name: Sofala Trading Port
sub_clusters.description: Sofala emerges as major gold export port linking Great Zimbabwe interior to Indian Ocean trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Kilwa-Sofala Gold Trade
sub_clusters.description: Kilwa Sultanate controls Sofala gold trade; Mozambican coast as southern reach of Swahili civilisation.

sub_clusters.name: Island of Mozambique
sub_clusters.description: Ilha de Moçambique as Swahili trading settlement before Portuguese arrival; Arab and Bantu cultural synthesis.

920.name: Great Zimbabwe and Interior Trade Networks
920.description: Mozambican coast as export corridor for gold, ivory, and copper from Great Zimbabwe and successor states.

sub_clusters.name: Great Zimbabwe Gold Corridor
sub_clusters.description: Trade routes from Great Zimbabwe plateau through Save River valley to Sofala port.

sub_clusters.name: Mutapa Empire Trade Links
sub_clusters.description: Kingdom of Mutapa controls gold-producing regions; trade via Zambezi and coastal Mozambique.

930.name: Portuguese Colonisation Begins
930.description: Vasco da Gama reaches Mozambique 1498; Portuguese establish forts, prazos (estates), and attempt to control gold trade.

sub_clusters.name: Vasco da Gama Arrives
sub_clusters.description: Da Gama lands at Ilha de Moçambique 1498; Portuguese establish fort at Sofala 1505.

sub_clusters.name: Prazo Estate System
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese crown land grants (prazos) in Zambezi valley; Afro-Portuguese warlord culture; slave armies (achikunda).

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Wars with Mutapa
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese military expeditions to control Mutapa gold fields; Battle of Maungwe; eventual Mutapa vassalage.

940.name: Late Colonial Mozambique
940.description: Mozambique becomes separate colony; slave trade peaks; chartered companies; forced labour (chibalo); Estado Novo repression.

sub_clusters.name: Slave Trade from Mozambique
sub_clusters.description: Mozambique becomes major Indian Ocean slave export zone; Quelimane and Ibo as departure points.

sub_clusters.name: Chartered Companies Era
sub_clusters.description: Mozambique Company, Niassa Company, and Zambezia Company effectively govern territory; forced labour and exploitation.

sub_clusters.name: Chibalo Forced Labour System
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese forced labour system; migrant workers sent to South African mines and Rhodesian farms.

sub_clusters.name: Estado Novo in Mozambique
sub_clusters.description: Salazar's New State regime; Mozambique as 'overseas province'; settler colonialism intensifies; cotton forced cultivation.

950.name: FRELIMO and Liberation War
950.description: FRELIMO founded; armed struggle begins 1964; Mondlane assassinated; Machel leads to independence 1975.

sub_clusters.name: FRELIMO Founded
sub_clusters.description: Eduardo Mondlane unites three movements into FRELIMO in Dar es Salaam; armed struggle begins 25 September 1964.

sub_clusters.name: Liberation War 1964-1974
sub_clusters.description: Guerrilla war in northern Mozambique; Mondlane assassinated 1969; Samora Machel assumes leadership.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Mozambique
sub_clusters.description: Carnation Revolution in Lisbon; Lusaka Accord; independence 25 June 1975; Machel first president.

950.name: Mozambican Civil War
950.description: RENAMO insurgency backed by Rhodesia and apartheid South Africa; devastating 16-year civil war; 1 million dead.

sub_clusters.name: RENAMO Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Rhodesian-then South African-backed RENAMO wages brutal insurgency; massive displacement and famine.

sub_clusters.name: Rome General Peace Accords
sub_clusters.description: Italian-mediated peace negotiations; General Peace Accord signed 4 October 1992; UN peacekeeping.

960.name: Post-War Reconstruction and Modern Mozambique
960.description: Democratic elections; economic growth; gas discoveries; Cabo Delgado insurgency; climate vulnerability.

sub_clusters.name: Multiparty Elections
sub_clusters.description: First democratic elections 1994; FRELIMO dominant party; disputed elections; RENAMO demilitarises.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Growth and Megaprojects
sub_clusters.description: Aluminium smelting (Mozal); coal exports; natural gas discoveries in Rovuma Basin; FDI surge.

sub_clusters.name: Cabo Delgado Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Islamist insurgency in Cabo Delgado province; attacks on Mocímboa da Praia and Palma; SADC intervention.

sub_clusters.name: Climate Vulnerability and Cyclones
sub_clusters.description: Cyclone Idai (2019) and Kenneth devastate central Mozambique; flooding; climate adaptation challenges.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
